dedupe_keys.name: global refinery infrastructure and petroleum trade data 2020 capshaw and padgett designsafe

description: This dataset gives the locations and daily processing capacities of the world's petroleum refineries operating in 2020, and the 2020 trade flow volumes of crude oil and petroleum products between 15 major world regions. The DesignSafe page says it was built for global risk and reliability assessment of refining and of the crude and product distribution network under hazard-induced disruptions, and was used to model disruption risk from extreme coastal floods under current and future climate. It was published on 7 June 2022 by Kendall Capshaw and Jamie Padgett as three CSV files (refineries about 34 KB, crude trade flows and product trade flows about 1 KB each) and a readme, free to download under the Open Data Commons Attribution licence. Coverage is worldwide at facility level for refineries and at 15-region level for trade. Caveats: it is a 2020 snapshot, trade is aggregated to regions, not ports or countries, and the sources of capacities are described only in the readme and the related papers. For simulation it gives a ready refinery layer and regional flow network to test how flooding of coastal refineries cuts product supply between regions. Related catalogue records include the virtual oil refinery seismic testbed, the global site-specific health impacts of fossil plants and refineries, and UN Comtrade.
